Latest Change: 26. May 2026 - is now more noticable ahead on pure single target, the hero talent requires 1100 haste. A switch is advised if you can get the haste requirement on single target heavy encounetrs like Midnight Falls.

Subtlety Rogue Rotation in 

The rotation for Subtlety Rogue is based on cooldowns combined with two resources you need to manage. The basis is a builder-and-spender system, where combo point builders generate combo points. Finishers are used to consume these combo points when close to the maximum amount (6 or 7 combo points). Energy is the limiting resource most of the time, and it's completely normal to feel resource-starved. Cooldowns allow you to accelerate the cycle and give access to stronger builders, creating a damage profile with serious damage during cooldowns and very low outside.

 Resource economy: Energy and Combo Point income varies a lot on Subtlety, the generation of both resources is low outside of cooldowns but high during. The passive talent Shadow Techniques is responsible for a big part of the income; this makes staying within auto attack range essential in both single target and AoE situations. The pacing outside of cooldowns can feel slow as a result.
 

 Cooldown Management: The vast majority of damage is bound to cooldowns, offering Subtlety the unique opportunity to stack them. All cooldowns are aligned to Secret Technique, which means we only use Shadow Dance when the spell is ready. Our major cooldown Shadow Blades is used alongside Shadow Dance when possible, and a second instance of Shadow Dance is typically used right after the first ended (the second cast won't have Secret Technique ready). Cooldowns don't line up well naturally, which often means we delay both Secret Technique and Shadow Dance slightly when Shadow Blades is about to come off cooldown.
 

 Global Cooldown Efficiency: All of Subtleties damage is in Cooldowns, which means utilizing every second becomes essential. Make sure not to cast Shadow Dance during a global cooldown and use your first ability as soon as possible after. This is important because of the Deepening Shadows talent, which can extend the duration of Shadow Dance just enough to fit another spell. Any small delay can lead to a loss here. A common strategy to prevent this is the use of a macro that combines the cooldown with a combo point builder or spender. 

Subtlety Rogue Starter Guide

 Best Subtlety Rogue Rotation

Subtleties' main priority is managing cooldowns while trying to be resource-efficient. This concentrates as much damage as possible into our cooldown windows.

Opener Sequence

 Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Subtlety Rogue to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

(Lethal Poison) Instant Poison - You will almost always want to use this poison for damage.
(Lethal Poison) Wound Poison - Can be used in Mythic+ in areas with a lot of mobs with self-healing abilities, like the initial zone in Gambit.
( Utility Poison) Atrophic Poison - Is the priority choice in Raiding and Mythic+.
( Utility Poison) Numbing Poison - It is advised to use this instead of Atrophic Poison if there is a 2nd rogue in your Raid team to get the benefit of both effects. This poison is also fairly good in Mythic+ in general and a valid choice and alternative to Atrophic Poison in dungeons with a lot of casting enemies.
( Utility Poison) Crippling Poison - Is usually not used.

(Mythic+ & Raids) Apply Weapon Oils Use Thalassian Phoenix Oil on both weapons. (only need to be re-applied if they are about to run out)
(Mythic+ & Raids) Eat Buff Food and drink Flasks. (only if you need to reapply them or if the buffs are about to run out)
(Optional) Prepare Supercharger Charges - The first two charges don't reset on encounter or dungeon start, we can exploit this by using Shadow Dance before a pull/key start.

 Subtlety Rogue Major Cooldowns

Subtlety has access to a variety of different cooldowns. All of them come with some extra wrinkles in how they work rather than simply being flat increases, so the below section covers how they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.

 Secret Technique‎ 

Secret Technique is a finishing move that's split in three parts, and is the only cooldown on Subtlety that has a static cooldown, which is reduced by haste. The following information is good to know:

Optimal Use

The optimal use of Secret Technique is during Shadow Dance as soon as possible. 

Shadow Dance 

Shadow Dance is the defining cooldown of Subtlety and allows the use of Stealth specific spells for its duration. Many talents hook into it, passively increasing damage output, the duration, or giving other benefits in addition to that. The list below highlights some unique aspects:

Optimal Use

You always want to use Shadow Dance with either very low combo points or finishing combo points. 
 - Prefers to start Shadow Dance with low combo points.
 - Prefers to start Shadow Dance with finishing combo points.

Only use it if Secret Technique is ready (not on cooldown).
Shadow Dance should be used a second time during Shadow Blades without Secret Technique ready; it is advised not to use Shadow Dance when Shadow Blades has less than 10 second remaining to ensure two casts when it's ready.

Optimization: Tier set 4p bonus in combination with Light Company Guidon:
Delaying your second Shadow Dance cast during Shadow Blades is beneficial. Use Shadow Dance once Shadow Blades has 8 seconds of duration left. 

Shadow Blades

Shadow Blades is a 90-second cooldown that doubles the combo point generation of your combo point building spells. It also echos 20% of the damage done by spells used during its uptime as shadow damage. The list below lists some additional facts about the spell which might be relevant.

Optimal Use

Use with Shadow Blades with Shadow Dance.

 Subtlety Rogue Advanced Tips

This section talks about optional ways to increase your damage or reliability. You don't need to do these optimizations when learning, but you might want to take a look once you feel comfortable with the rotation basics.

 The haste problem, and how to solve it.

 Deepening Shadows increases the duration of Shadow Dance based on your haste value; the amount of extra time can be very low, making it important to use spells as soon as possible. 

 The following is advised in order to minimize impact:
 As : Use a macro with Secret Technique and Shadow Dance.
As : Use a macro with Shuriken Storm and Shadow Dance. 
General: Don't use Shadow Dance during a Global Cooldown.

 You can find this and other macros in the macro and ui guide.

 Apex talents.

The apex talents increase damage during cooldowns even more, which leads to optimizations that don't seem intuitive. 

Optimizations

The table below highlights optimizations:
You can stop using finishing moves a few seconds before Secret Technique comes off cooldown. 
Both Hero talents want to optimize around Ancient Arts during Shadow Dance. This means using Shadowstrike on high combo points to activate the effect if its not up. More specifics in the list below.
As : Try to have your supercharged Eviscerate or Black Powder empowered by Ancient Arts.
As : Always try to get Ancient Arts for your Darkest Night - Eviscerate cast on up to 4 targets. 

Our Subtlety Rogue guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on View Changelog in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Subtlety Rogue guides for , make sure to browse the Navigation Bar at the top of the page, along with our list of Related Guides just beneath the Table of Contents.

Notes will appear here.
Shadowstrike is always used from Stealth or Vanish. Shadowstrike teleports you to the target if used this way. This is handy when you want to close the gap to a new pack in Mythic+ faster.
Secret Technique is your top priority finisher during Shadow Dance and used as soon as possible.
Low combo points more specifically refers to one or fewer. You can use Shadow Dance with your high combo points (6 or 7) to finish immediately after, but low combo points are typically better. This spell is your central cooldown, and sensitive to input lag, so make sure not to use it during a global cooldown to be able to fill every global possible.
You usually want to use Shadow Dance with your high combo points (6 or 7) to finish immediately after, but low combo points (0 or 1) are fine too. This spell is your central cooldown, and sensitive to input lag, so make sure not to use it during a global cooldown to be able to fill every global possible.
This is a fall back option to re-apply Deathstalker's Mark, which is typically done with Shadowstrike. The use of Eviscerate is rare as a consequence, making this mostly relevant for pulls that last longer or sustained AoE.
The use of Shadowstrike would be ideal, but does not work in a macro now. This introduces a short delay between Shadow Dance and the cast of Shadow Dance. The delay is dependent on your latency and is at least 100ms. This is enough to make Shuriken Storm a good alternative. Shuriken Storm gets empowered by Shadow Dance(200% damage) ,Silent Storm(100% chance to critical hit), procs Danse Macabre and generates full combo points thanks to Premeditation. This combined allows it to be close enough in output to use the macro for reliability.
When using this macro, always make sure to be on 6 or 7 combo points before using Shadow Dance. It is better to stop using finishers ~3-4 seconds before Secret Technique comes off cooldown than to delay the use of the macro.
The reason we use Shuriken Storm and not Shadowstrike is a bug introduced in Dragonflight. This bug would require two key presses, which adds at minimum the amount of lag between you and the server to the cast. This reduces reliability. Using Shuriken Storm is a good enough alternative due to the many talents that increase its damage and make the cast a guaranteed critical strike.

A good way to test if you need this macro or not is to play your rotation on a target dummy, if you notice barely missing your last cast in Shadow Dance or if you get the animation of an Shadowstrike attack but not the attack, use the macro approach.

Not using finishers generates additional stacks of Shadow Techniques, leading to slightly more procs of the last apex effect. 

Doing so also reduces potential delays introduced by building up combo points when playing (So you can use Shadow Dance and Secret Technique as soon as both are ready without delay).

The apex talents procs when you have 5+ stacks of Shadow Techniques. You don't want to empower Secret Technique because of how it interacts with the Apex talents. 

You might want to use the checklist below to determine when to use Shadowstrike on high combo points:
Is Shadow Dance up? - Yes
Do you have 5 or more stacks of Shadow Techniques? - Yes
Do you have at least 1 Supercharger combo point? - Yes
Is Secret Technique ready? - NO
Is Ancient Arts up? - NO

Use Shadowstrike if all conditions are fulfilled.

The apex talents procs when you have 5+ stacks of Shadow Techniques. You want to have the apex proc on Darkest Night empowered Eviscerate. But only on up to 4 targets.

You might want to use the checklist below to determine when to use Shadowstrike on high combo points:
Is Shadow Dance up? - Yes
Do you have 5 or more stacks of Shadow Techniques? - Yes
Is your next finisher Eviscerate? - Yes
Is Ancient Arts up? - NO

Use Shadowstrike if all conditions are fulfilled.

Two-target cleave is a special case. Using Eviscerate instead of Black Powder is stronger when you are not talented in Potent Powder. The difference with the talent is minor, making both abilities valid to use with exactly two targets. 

Black Powder is stronger on 3+ targets, and as such, the default choice on most encounters with adds/multi-target cleave.

Delaying your second Shadow Dance allows it to fit Secret Technique in it, increasing your overall output.

The mentioned optimization is reliable and easy to perform; you can squeeze out just another minimal increase by doing the following:

You want to have supercharger on both casts of Secret Technique during Shadow Blades. This means delaying your second Shadow Dance till Secret Technique has 2 secounds of cooldown left. This allows you to use it as second finisher during the duration.

The best trinkets for single target are on-use trinkets; the best ones are tricky to use.
The list below outlines the use of the specific trinkets:

Light Company Guidon, Emberwing Feather - Use them one second before your major cooldowns and Shadow Dance. This is a consequence of how Deepening Shadows works. The duration is only updated in intervals of one second, which has a risk of losing the benefits when used with Shadow Dance.
Algeth'ar Puzzle Box - Is a two-second channel. Use it before going into Major cooldowns. (The trinket is used as if it has a 3-minute cooldown)

The most likely trinket to use in Mythic+ is Algeth'ar Puzzle Box. The trinket has a two-second channel, and as such, it is best to be used before major cooldowns. This means using the trinket after Shadow Strike before going into cooldown. The trinket is used as if the cooldown is 3 minutes.

Shuriken Storm does decent amount of damage from talents like Clear the Witnesses, Silent Storm and the double damage bonus from Shadow Dance. The spell also procs Danse Macabre. Everything combined makes using Shuriken Storm already considerable, but the main reason we use it is the duration increase of Shadow Dance via the talent Deepening Shadows. This increase can be small enough to miss the last cast during Shadow Dance barely. To avoid this problem, we macro Shuriken Storm with Shadow Dance and use this macro as our shadow dance trigger.

The easiest way to play it is to just create a macro for Shuriken Storm with Shadow Dance and make sure to use the macro only when low on combo points.

actions.race+=/invoke_external_buff,name=power_infusion,if=variable.racial_sync

# Trinket and Items
actions.item=potion,if=buff.shadow_blades.up|fight_remains<30
actions.item+=/use_item,name=algethar_puzzle_box,if=cooldown.shadow_blades.ready&cooldown.secret_technique.remains<=2&combo_points>=6
actions.item+=/use_items,slots=trinket1,if=(variable.trinket_sync_slot=1&(buff.shadow_blades.up|fight_remains<=20)|(variable.trinket_sync_slot=2&(!trinket.2.cooldown.ready&cooldown.shadow_blades.remains>20))|!variable.trinket_sync_slot)
actions.item+=/use_items,slots=trinket2,if=(variable.trinket_sync_slot=2&(buff.shadow_blades.up|fight_remains<=20)|(variable.trinket_sync_slot=1&(!trinket.1.cooldown.ready&cooldown.shadow_blades.remains>20))|!variable.trinket_sync_slot)

actions.finish=eviscerate,if=buff.darkest_night.up
actions.finish+=/secret_technique,if=buff.shadow_dance.up|(cooldown.secret_technique.duration<18|cooldown.shadow_dance.remains>=10)&!cooldown.shadow_dance.ready
actions.finish+=/coup_de_grace,if=cooldown.secret_technique.remains>=3|buff.shadow_dance.up
actions.finish+=/black_powder,if=variable.targets>=3
# Pool some Shadow Technique Stacks before entering Shadow Dance by not finishing right before.
actions.finish+=/eviscerate,if=cooldown.secret_technique.remains>=3&talent.unseen_blade|buff.shadow_dance.up|buff.shadow_blades.up|debuff.deathstalkers_mark.stack>1|debuff.deathstalkers_mark.stack=1&buff.shadow_techniques.stack>=5

actions.build=shuriken_storm,if=prev.shadow_dance&buff.premeditation.up&talent.danse_macabre
actions.build+=/shadowstrike,if=!debuff.deathstalkers_mark.up&talent.deathstalkers_mark&!buff.darkest_night.up|variable.targets<=3|variable.priority_rotation
actions.build+=/shuriken_storm,if=variable.targets>1
actions.build+=/goremaws_bite,if=combo_points.deficit>=3
actions.build+=/gloomblade,if=variable.targets<2&!variable.stealth
actions.build+=/backstab,if=variable.targets<2&!variable.stealth

# This list usually contains Cooldowns with negligible impact that causes global cooldowns
actions.fill=arcane_torrent,if=energy.deficit>=15+energy.regen
actions.fill+=/arcane_pulse
actions.fill+=/lights_judgment
actions.fill+=/bag_of_tricks
